Vocabulary Pool Choose which words go into the game.

Lessons and Categories hold the same words, just organised differently. Lessons groups them by lesson number; Categories groups them by part of speech, so you can practise only Verbs, only Nouns, and so on.

⭐ uses the words you've starred. Tap the ☆ beside any word in the Vocabulary menu to add it here.
Pool: 0 words
Direction Choose what you hear and what you tap.

Thai → English: You hear the Thai word and tap its English card.

English → Thai: You hear the English word and tap its Thai card.

Mixed: Each card is randomly Thai or English, and you hear the opposite side.
Lives How many wrong taps you can afford. Each miss costs one life; reach zero and the game ends. 1 life is sudden death.
Layout Choose the grid size for your game. Every card is unique — there are no pairs — so the number shown is the total number of cards. Wide layouts work best on phones held horizontally; narrow layouts work best held vertically.

Sentence Pool Pick which lessons the sentences come from. Tap a lesson chip to include or exclude it; the counter shows how many sentences are in your current selection.
Pool: 0 sentences
English Hint When on, the English meaning is shown above the scrambled words as a clue. Turn it off for a tougher challenge — rebuild the Thai sentence from the words alone.
Lives How many wrong sentences you can afford. Each incorrect arrangement costs one life; reach zero and the game ends. 1 life is sudden death.
Spoken Answer When on, the full sentence is read aloud in Thai after you check it — both when you get it right and (as a hint) when you get it wrong but still have a life left. You can also press and hold any word card to hear its pronunciation.
Sentences per session How many sentences to build in one game. The game ends when you finish them all (a win) or run out of lives.

Memory Game

ℹ️ Choose a layout (e.g. 5×4), select an opponent, and click START to begin.

Computer opponents will occasionally greet you, comment on matches, or react to misses. These conversations are a fun way to learn useful everyday phrases. If you find them distracting, set In-Game Popups to Streak or OFF.


You can view all computer opponent lines in the Vocabulary menu under the Computer tab.

Adjust the game speed anytime in Settings menu if the game feels too fast or too slow.

Settings

การตั้งค่า gaan dtâng kâa

Display Choose what's shown on the Thai-language cards.

Thai + Roman: Shows both the Thai script and its romanization (a phonetic spelling using the alphabet). Best for beginners.

Thai only: Hides the romanization, so you practise reading the script.

Roman only: Hides the Thai script, so you practise the pronunciation.
Speed Memory Games: How long unmatched cards stay flipped before turning back over, and how quickly computer opponents take their turns.

Audio Bingo: The pause before the next word is spoken.

Connect Pairs: The pause after each matched pair.

A slower speed gives you more time to read and memorize.
After Matching a Pair What happens to a pair once it has been matched. Affects Memory Games, Audio Bingo and Connect Pairs.

Keep visible: Matched cards stay on the board, faded out.

Remove cards: Matched cards fade away, so the board gets less crowded as you go.
Card Back Choose the artwork shown on the back of each card. Only affects the Memory Games (Solo Play, Play vs Computer and Multiplayer).

Tone Trainer

Pronunciation Practice

ฝึกวรรณยุกต์ fèuk wan-na-yúk

Getting Started

The Tone Trainer lets you practise your Thai tones. You speak a word into the microphone, and the app shows the shape of your pitch and tells you which of the five tones it heard — rising, falling, mid, high, or low.

Before you start, you’ll set up a quick voice profile (about half a minute). This is a one-time step that makes tone detection much more accurate for your voice.

A profile records your natural speaking pitch, so the app knows where your low, mid, and high sit. Here’s how:

  1. Make sure you’re in a quiet room.
  2. Tap “＋ Add profile” below.
  3. Enter your name and tap Next.
  4. Tap Record (allow microphone access if asked), then read the sentence shown. Speak naturally.
  5. Once your profile is saved, tap Start to begin practising.

💡 You can make a profile for each person who uses the app, and recalibrate any time from the trainer screen.

⚠️ Never use another person's tone profile. Each profile is calibrated to one person's voice. Using someone else's profile can lead to inaccurate tone detection. If a friend wants to try the app, create and calibrate a profile for them first.

Voice Profile A voice profile records your natural speaking pitch once (about half a minute) so the trainer knows where your low, mid, and high tones sit. This makes tone detection far more accurate. Each learner should make their own profile — handy when more than one person shares the app.
Voice: —
Guide
  1. Find a quiet room.
  2. Click “Tap to speak” and say any single Thai word. There's no need to tap the button again—the recording will stop automatically when you finish speaking. See Useful words to practice below for suggestions.
  3. You’ll see your pitch shape, and the app will tell you which tone it heard.
  4. Optionally turn on a Guide Overlay for a visual hint of the tone you're trying to pronounce.
  5. Once you're comfortable with free practice, head back to the main menu and try the Tone Challenge game to test your skills.

⚠️ Detecting tones from pitch is not foolproof — the app can make mistakes. Don’t fully trust its result. Use it as guidance to point you in the right direction, but always double-check with a native speaker that your tones are understandable.

Tap any Thai word to hear it. Try saying it, and see if the app detects the right tone.

💡 The classic trio:
  • มา maa — to come (mid tone)
  • หมา măa — dog (rising tone)
  • ม้า máa — horse (high tone)
Mid เสียงสามัญ sĭang săa-man
  • ไป bpai — to go
  • นม nom — milk
  • กิน gin — to eat
Low เสียงเอก sĭang èk
  • ไก่ gài — chicken
  • ถูก tòok — cheap
  • ใหญ่ yài — big
Falling เสียงโท sĭang toh
  • บ้าน bâan — home; house
  • ได้ dâai — can
  • ห้า hâa — five (5)
High เสียงตรี sĭang dtree
  • รถ rót — car; vehicle
  • รัก rák — to love
  • น้ำ náam — water
Rising เสียงจัตวา sĭang jàt-dtà-waa
  • ผม pŏm — I (male)
  • สวย sŭay — beautiful
  • หิว hĭw — to be hungry

Ready

💡 Tap the button once and say a single Thai word (not a full sentence). The recording will stop automatically when you finish speaking and your detected tone will be shown.

Guide Overlay (optional) This only changes the faint dashed shape drawn behind your pitch line — a visual reference for what each Thai tone should look like. It’s purely cosmetic and does not affect tone detection. Choose “Off” for a clean graph, or pick a tone to overlay its ideal shape while you practise.

Cosmetic only — shows the ideal shape behind your line. Detection above is automatic.

The graph shows the shape of your pitch (up, down, flat) and where it sits in your range — high tones above the line, low tones below. Works best in a quiet room. If the centre line feels off for your voice, tap “Back” to return to the profile screen and recalibrate.

Debug mode records what the app measured for each attempt. Pick the tone you’re trying to say, record it, repeat for each tone a few times, then Copy or Download the log and send it. Nothing is uploaded automatically.

Tone Challenge

Pronunciation Practice

ฝึกวรรณยุกต์ fèuk wan-na-yúk

Getting Started

The Tone Challenge drills your Thai tones. The app shows a word, you say it into the microphone, and it scores how well your pitch matched the word’s tone — across a run of words for a final result.

You’ll use the same voice profile as the Tone Trainer. Pick one below (or add a new one) to begin.

During a run you can tap the Thai word to hear it spoken. This uses your device’s built-in text-to-speech, which often doesn’t reproduce Thai tones accurately — treat it as a rough aid, not a reliable pronunciation reference.

Voice Profile A voice profile records your natural speaking pitch once (about half a minute) so the app knows where your low, mid, and high tones sit. Profiles are shared with the Tone Trainer — calibrate once, use in both.
Words to drill How many words you’ll be asked to say in one challenge. Each word is scored, and your results are combined into a final rating at the end.
